endangerment.comment: Ndebele (nbl-nbl) = 1 (National). Statutory national language (1996, Constitution, Article 6(1)). Statutory provincial language in Mpumalunga province (2012, Use of Official Languages Act, No. 12, Section 4(1)).

hh_ethnologue_comment.comment: Ndebele [nbl] is listed in E16/E17/E18/E19/E20/E21/E22/E23/E24/E25/E26/E27/E28/E29 as a separate language of South Africa. In addition to Ndebele [nde] in Zimbabwe, the term Ndebele in South Africa may refer to two different groups. One may be called South Transvaal Ndebele or IsiNdebele and is spoken in Mpumalanga and Gauteng provinces (**hh:sv:Skhosana:Ndebele**, **hh:s:Jiyane:IsiNdebele**), and the other can be called North Transvaal Ndebele or Sumayela Ndebele or SiNdebele and is spoken in Limpopo province (**hh:sv:Skhosana:Ndebele**, **hh:g:Ziervogel:Northern-Transvaal-Ndebele**, **hh:soc:Jallow:Sindebele**). South Transvaal Ndebele may be linguistically classified as a Zulu dialect while North Transvaal Ndebele is a more distant separate Nguni language (**hh:hv:Ownby:Nguni**). The information in the Ndebele [nbl] entry is consistent only with South Transvaal Ndebele. But South Transvaal Ndebele, from a purely linguistic perspective, should be merged with Zulu [zul]. Furthermore, the North Transvaal Ndebele which does merit its own entry, has none, given the conflicting data in Ndebele [nbl]. See also: Zimbabwean Ndebele [nde], Zulu [zul].
